title: SNMP Enumeration Runner — Network Device Configuration and Asset Discovery
goal: Query network devices via SNMP to enumerate system information, network interfaces, routing tables, connected devices, and identify devices using default community strings.
scope: Create workers/runners/snmp_enum/runner.py. For each host with port 161 open (UDP): (1) TEST COMMUNITY STRINGS: try community strings 'public', 'private', 'community', 'manager', 'admin', 'snmpd', 'cisco', 'ubiquiti'. If any succeeds, create MEDIUM finding 'SNMP community string accepted' — default strings are a security risk. (2) SYSTEM ENUMERATION: if authenticated, walk OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1 (sysDescr, sysName, sysContact, sysLocation, sysUpTime). This identifies: Unifi switches/APs (sysDescr contains 'UniFi'), routers (sysDescr contains model name), NAS devices, managed switches. (3) INTERFACE ENUMERATION: walk OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2 (ifTable) to get all network interfaces, IP addresses, and MAC addresses. This reveals connected subnets, VLAN interfaces, and bridge interfaces. (4) ARP TABLE: walk OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.22 (ipNetToMediaTable) to get the full ARP cache — this reveals all hosts the device has seen, including IoT devices not directly reachable. (5) ROUTING TABLE: walk OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.21 to get routes and discover connected/known subnets. Use pysnmp library. Add profile passive-lan-snmp-enum: passive, targets all hosts in scope on UDP/161.
generation_reason: Unifi APs, switches, routers, NAS devices, and many IoT gateways respond to SNMP. The ARP table from a gateway router reveals ALL devices on the network including those that don't respond to pings. Current AegisPT has no SNMP capability despite settings referencing it.

constraints.scope_creep_guard: Read-only SNMP walks only. No SNMP write operations. Community string list limited to 9 known defaults. No SNMP bruteforce.
